claim: Heston-Jones-Khorram-Li-Mo (Jan 1996-Jun 2019, OptionMetrics, optionable common stocks): zero-delta ATM straddles on single stocks, 1-month expiry, held to expiration (unhedged static; daily-hedged variants also shown), entered at bid-ask midpoint (no costs in headline). Straddles with high returns over the prior 6-36 months keep outperforming; the effect holds for static and delta-hedged returns. Option momentum is about the OPTION's own past return, not the stock's past return.
quote: options with high historical returns continue to significantly outperform options with low historical returns over horizons ranging from 6 to 36 months.
title: Option Momentum (Heston, Jones, Khorram, Li, Mo), Sept 2021 draft

claim: Same study: after paying the full bid-ask spread, average option-momentum returns are close to zero for options with below-median bid-ask spreads (1-month ATM straddles, Jan 1996-Jun 2019), so the gross effect is largely consumed by costs.
quote: Average option momentum returns are close to zero after paying the full bid-ask spread for options with below-median bid-ask spreads.
title: Option Momentum (Heston et al.)

claim: Same study: 1-12 month formation quintile spread on static ATM 1-month straddles earned 3.64% per month (gross, mid-price, Jan 1996-Jun 2019), 5.59% per month when daily delta-hedged; hedged results are not an outright buyer's return.
quote: the 1-12 month static straddle quintile spread earned 3.64% per month, whereas its daily-hedged counterpart earned 5.59%
title: Option Momentum (Heston et al.)

claim: Same study: short formation horizons (1 or 1-2 months) of past straddle returns show negative reversal in static (unhedged) straddle returns, not continuation; the delta-hedged versions show continuation at all horizons.
quote: Instead of positive continuation, these short-term strategies display negative reversal.
title: Option Momentum (Heston et al.)

claim: Cao-Han-Tong-Zhan (sample Jan 1996-Dec 2012, ~50-day ATM options, price >= $5, daily-rebalanced delta-hedged gains held one month; HEDGED, mid-price, no costs in headline): hedged option gains increase with size, momentum, reversal and profitability and decrease with analyst forecast dispersion, new issuance and idiosyncratic volatility, though these variables do not predict stock returns in the sample.
quote: Delta-hedged option gains increase with size, momentum, reversal, and profitability and decrease with cash holding, analyst forecast dispersion, new issues, and idiosyncratic volatility
title: Option Return Predictability (Cao, Han, Tong, Zhan), April 2016 working paper

claim: Same paper: lagged 1-month return RET(-1,0) and 2-12 month return RET(-12,-2) predict stock returns in the opposite direction, yet both negatively predict the return to delta-neutral call WRITING, i.e. higher past stock return goes with higher delta-hedged gain for the option BUYER (hedged, Jan 1996-Dec 2012, ~50-day ATM). Mean pooled delta-hedged ATM call gain is negative (-1.03% over one month).
quote: short-term reversal (RET(-1,0)) and momentum (RET(-12,-2)) predict the future stock return in the opposite direction, while both negatively predict the return to delta-neutral call writing.
title: Option Return Predictability (Cao et al.)

claim: Same paper: the pooled average delta-hedged ATM call gain is -1.03% over the next month and -1.26% if held to maturity (about 50 calendar days), Jan 1996-Dec 2012 (hedged, mid-price).
quote: the pooled delta-hedged option gains on average are negative for both call and put options.
title: Option Return Predictability (Cao et al.)

claim: Same paper: sorted-portfolio profits shrink monotonically as assumed effective option spread rises from 0 (mid) to 100% of the quoted spread; average quoted bid-ask for the ATM options is about 20% (median 15.6%).
quote: the equal-weighed (10-1) return spread to delta-neutral call writing decreases monotonically with the transaction costs.
title: Option Return Predictability (Cao et al.)

claim: Choy & Wei (Financial Review 2022; abstract only read, sample/maturity not seen): subsequent DELTA-HEDGED option returns for both calls and puts are higher as the stock price approaches its 52-week high or low; option traders appear to anchor on the 52-week extreme. Hedged, costs and maturity not stated in abstract.
quote: the subsequent delta‐hedged option returns for both calls and puts are higher as the stock price approaches its 52‐week extreme.
title: Option trading and returns versus the 52-week high and low (Choy, Wei), Financial Review

claim: Choi & Jayaraman (Jan 1996-Dec 2004; SHARE returns, window 2 days only): after one-day declines of 10% or more, the two-day CAR is -0.24% for optionable NYSE/AMEX firms and 0.06% for optionable NASDAQ firms, versus +0.72% and +0.78% for non-optionable firms. No 1-6 month horizon, no option returns, sample ends 2004 (pre-2015).
quote: are 0.72 per cent, while those of optionable NYSE/AMEX firms are -0.24 per cent.
title: Is Reversal of Large Stock-Price Declines Caused by Overreaction or Information Asymmetry (Choi, Jayaraman), Feb 2008 draft

claim: Choi & Jayaraman sample: daily CRSP stocks and OptionMetrics data, Jan 1996-Dec 2004 (ends before 2015); event is a stock price decline of 10% or more.
quote: the sample period for our study is from January 1996 through December 2004.
title: Choi & Jayaraman 2008 draft
